output.subject: Your credit limit decrease
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us about the change to your credit limit.

You told us your credit line was reduced to $2,000 and that the only notice you received was a form letter. You also mentioned that you pay your balance in full most months, so we understand why this change came as a surprise and why you were unhappy with how you learned about it. We're sorry for the frustration this has caused.

You've asked two things: exactly what triggered the decrease, and how you can get your previous limit back. We've passed your message and both of those questions to our Card Services team, who will review the circumstances you've described.

We will respond within 10 business days with a reply that addresses each of your questions. If you have any further details you'd like us to consider in the meantime, such as the date of the letter you received, please reply to this email.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Confirm the limit decrease, the new $2,000 limit, and the date it took effect.
Check what notice was sent (the form letter), when, and whether it stated a reason for the decrease.
Decide what reason for the decrease can be shared with the customer.
Decide whether a limit restoration or reconsideration is available and how the customer would request it.
Customer included a mobile number; decide whether a call-back is appropriate (number withheld from the draft).
Customer did not state the previous limit; verify it before referring to it.
